gloss: things seen and heard; experience; observations; knowledge gained firsthand

forms.negative: {見聞|みき}きしていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {見聞|みき}きしていませんでした

definitions.gloss: things seen and heard; experience; observations; knowledge gained firsthand
definitions.explanation: Knowledge and impressions acquired through direct personal observation, such as what one witnessed and learned during travel or fieldwork.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}での{見聞|みき}きを{話|はな}した。
examples.english: I talked about what I saw and heard on the trip.

examples.japanese: {見聞|みき}きを{広|ひろ}げるために{海外|かいがい}に{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: I went abroad to broaden my horizons.

examples.japanese: {現地|げんち}で{見聞|みき}きしたことをもとに、{報告書|ほうこくしょ}をまとめた。
examples.english: I compiled a report based on what I saw and heard on site.

notes:
Combines {見|み}る (to see) and {聞|き}く (to hear) to refer to firsthand experience and knowledge gained through direct observation. As a noun, it means the things one has seen and heard; as a verb ({見聞|みき}きする), it means to see and hear, to observe directly.

USAGE:
- {見聞|みき}きを{広|ひろ}げる is a very common expression meaning "to broaden one's experience/horizons"
- The kanji compound {見聞|けんぶん} is a more formal reading with the same meaning
- Often used when recounting travel experiences or field observations

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見聞|みき}きを{広|ひろ}げる: to broaden one's experience
- {見聞|みき}きしたこと: things one has seen and heard
- {見聞|みき}きを{深|ふか}める: to deepen one's knowledge through experience
- {見聞|みき}き{録|ろく}: a record of observations

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {経験|けいけん}: experience — broader, includes all types of experience
- {見聞|けんぶん}: the on'yomi reading; more formal and literary
- {体験|たいけん}: hands-on experience — emphasizes personal participation
